Yes, happy to help. Our goal today is to describe what people are doing right now, using am, is or are with a verb ending in -ing.

This is useful in daily life, for example when you tell a friend on the phone what is happening around you, or when you describe a scene you can see.

Let us start with what you already know. Look around you now, or imagine a busy street. Write one sentence about what one person is doing at this moment.

Yes, we can. Our goal today is to talk about amounts: things you can count one by one, and things you cannot count.

This is very useful in daily life, for example when you shop for food or cook with a friend.

Let us start with what you already know. Think of your own kitchen. Name one thing you can count one by one, and one thing you cannot count, such as a liquid or a powder.

Yes, of course. Our goal today is to join two short sentences into one, using and, but or because.

These small words make your writing smoother. For example, you will need them when you write a message to a neighbour or a colleague about your day.

Let us start with what you already know. Which of these three words do you use most often when you write, and what is one sentence where you used it? Write that sentence for me.

Yes, we can. Our goal today is to describe finished events in the past, using irregular verbs, which do not take -ed.

This helps in daily life when you tell someone what happened, for example at work, at the doctor or with a friend.

Let us start with what you already know. Think about yesterday. Write one or two sentences about something you did, and I will look at the verbs together with you.
